thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stock Market Set For Lower Open As Jobs Data Boost Yields

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stock Market Set For Lower Open As Jobs Data Boost Yields
text:
By Anora M. Gaudiano and Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch
Dow, S&P 500 face worst weekly performances since late 2016
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures fell but trimmed losses ahead of the bell on Friday, as investors digested a stronger-than-expected jobs report that saw bond yields continue their climb.
The U.S. economy added 200,000 jobs in January (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-adds-2 -jobs-worker-pay-rises-at-fastest-pace-since-2009-2018-02-02)with the best news coming from the wage growth. Average hourly wages rose 0.3%, the fastest pace in more than eight years.
Premarket gains for Amazon.com Inc. provided a bright spot after those companies delivered upbeat results, but appeared unable to do lift the main indexes that are now facing their worst weekly performance in more than a year.
What are the main benchmarks doing?
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures were down 188 points, or 0.7%, to 25,981, while S&P 500 futures slid 14.65 points, or 0.5%, to 2,807. Nasdaq-100 futures were off 16 points, or 0.3%, to 6,879.
Rising bond yields and concerns about higher inflation left stocks mostly lower on Thursday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/sp-500-poised-to-rise-lifted-by-ebay-surge-2018-02-01). The Dow Jones Industrial Average was an exception, rising 37.32 points, or 0.1%, to finish at 26,186.71, after shaking off a 135-point loss at one point in the session. The S&P 500 index slipped 0.1% to end at 2,821.98, while the Nasdaq Composite Index slid 25.62 points, or 0.4%, at 7,385.86.
A couple of bruising sessions this week have left their mark. The S&P 500 was down 1.8% on the week as of Thursday's close, set for its worst weekly performance since November 2016. The Dow average was facing a 1.6% weekly loss, its worst since September 2016. The Nasdaq Composite, meanwhile, was looking at a 1.6% loss, the deepest seen since last June.
What are strategists saying?
"The markets are coming to grip with the fact that a 3-3.25% yield factor is not far away. In summary. higher yields will continue to keep pressure on stocks," Peter Cardillo, chief market economist at First Standard Financial, said in a note to clients, referring to the 10-year Treasury rate.
 in Amazon Inc.(AMZN) climbed 5.7% in thin premarket trading after the e-commerce retailer posted fourth-quarter profit and revenue that blew past forecasts.

Shares of Amgen Inc. (AMGN) were set to fall for after the pharmaceutical company late Thursday reported fourth-quarter loss of $4.26 billion, or a loss of $5.89 per share, after earnings of $1.94 billion, or $2.59 per share in the year-earlier period, disappointing the street (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/amgen-shares-drop-4-after-q4-profit-revenue-misses-2018-02-01).
Exxon Mobil Corp.(XOM) earnings fell short of estimates, despite tax benefit. Shares were down 3% premarket.
Phillips 66 (PSX) shares were slightly higher after the company released earnings above Wall Street's expectations.
J.C. Penney Co.(JCP) earnings are all on the docket ahead of the bell.
What could help drive markets?
Stocks were taking a hit as global government bond yields, which have dogged stocks this week, continued to climb on Friday. The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note rose to a four-year high above 2.8%.
Meanwhile, the yield on 10-year German government bunds added 4 basis points to reach 0.690%, close to levels not seen in more than two years. Higher returns on debt securities tend to weaken appetite for stocks and other assets perceived as risky.
Read: U.S. jobs report in January likely to show meaty gain in hiring, low unemployment (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/january-jobs-bonanza-hiring-likely-rebounded-in-early-2018-2018-02-01)
(http://www.marketwatch.com/story/january-jobs-bonanza-hiring-likely-rebounded-in-early-2018-2018-02-01)Plus:A new report says the unemployment rate may have a lot more room to fall (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/back-to-the-1950s-a-new-report-says-the-unemployment-rate-may-have-a-lot-more-room-to-fall-2018-02-01)
Consumer sentiment for January is due at 10 a.m. Eastern, along with factory orders for December.
What are other assets doing?
European stocks slumped, driven by a 1.3% slide for the German DAX (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dax-drops-below-13000-after-deutsche-bank-logs-a-hefty-loss-2018-02-02), in part dogged by Deutsche Bank's hefty loss. Asian markets saw a mixed session, with the Nikkei 225 index down 0.9% on disappointing earnings. Gold was flat, while oil futures inched up, and the ICE U.S. Dollar Index rose to 88.85, thought it is still down 3.6% since the start of the year.
